Database: Native PostgreSQL verification database only; generated schemas and Redis namespaces cleaned
NotificationChecks: Authenticated owner list, global unread count and all read/delete mutations; anonymous access rejected
Each response includes actual recipient userId; optional X-FRAME-USER-ID mismatch rejects reads and writes before notification data access
B cookie and valid B CSRF with expected A header returns SESSION_CHANGED and leaves B rows/unread count unchanged
Foreign and missing notification IDs share 404; CSRF, Origin, malformed UUID/cursor/filter/limit checks enforced
Report terminal change and its generic private recipient notice share a transaction; rollback preserves original report and no notice
Report result includes public channel-name snapshot, receipt UUID and status, without report details, private review note, reviewer or account credentials
Existing live streams establish a baseline without historical alerts; only already-enabled followers receive new source starts
Midstream follow or OFF-to-ON does not create a past-start notification
Source/session and broadcast-instance markers suppress polling duplicates, deleted-row resurrection and short reconnects
New instance with the same source reserves its own marker; subsequent reconnect under that instance remains suppressed
Live body comes from server broadcast title with PostgreSQL NUL normalization
Live target availability requires current broadcast UUID/path/instance and fresh matching observed source; restart safely disables old targets
Equal-millisecond UUID keyset pagination, idempotent first-read timestamp, read-all and clear-all preserve exact owner unread totals
Notification rows survive a fresh Spring Boot instance without reviving old live links
Product-only isolated worker catches database errors and retries without throwing into media/registry threads
V7 preserves follow flags/dates, baselines enabled-at time and creates no historical user notifications
V1 through V6 SQL hashes unchanged; checksum mismatch blocks synthetic pending V8
Notes: API integration uses a controlled loopback MediaMTX API fixture; actual FFmpeg/RTMP browser QA is performed separately by the root agent
All application and database test data stayed inside generated verification schemas and Redis namespaces
No main API restart, real account grants, Docker execution, OS reboot or changes to active OBS/media processes were performed
No push/SSE, email, message broker, Redis queue or generic event framework was added
